title: Token-level observability: enhanced metrics, tracing, dashboards, and alert tuning
author: Avery Chen
release_notes: Adds token-level cost/latency breakdowns to observability dashboards; introduces sampled token tracing for high-latency traces; updates alert thresholds for token-level latency and cost regressions; no breaking changes.
description: Motivation: customers need better visibility into per-token cost and latency to diagnose regressions introduced by batching and model variants. This PR extends our token-level observability surface with actionable metrics, sampled tracing, and dashboard/alert tuning. Summary: 1) add new token-level metrics (token_count, token_latency_p50/p90/p99, token_cost_estimate) emitted per request and aggregated per-route/model; 2) implement sampled token-level tracing hooks that link to existing spanIDs without increasing normal trace volume (configurable sample rate); 3) dashboard updates for the Observability Console: per-model token breakdown, per-route cost/latency heatmaps, and a token regression page; 4) alert tuning: introduce new alert rules that trigger on sustained token P99 latency and unexpected token-cost-per-request increases; 5) migration: metrics are additive and use new metric namespaced keys to avoid collisions. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-5621) - [x] metrics schema and export implemented - [x] tracing sampler implemented with feature flag - [x] dashboards added to grafana repo - [x] alert rules added and tested in staging - [x] docs updated with examples What this changes (high level): emits new metrics to prometheus via pushgateway when in Dedicated/Private; on Hosted API metrics flow through our metrics pipeline to metrics-store and are available in console. Token tracing attaches a token.span subspan to the existing request span when sampled. Backwards compatibility: metric names are new and default sampling is 0.1% in production to avoid cost/noise; customers can opt-in to higher sampling in Dedicated/Private with config. Testing and QA: unit tests for metric tags, integration tests asserting dashboard panels render expected aggregates on synthetic workloads, e2e run in staging with 24h synthetic traffic to validate alert firing/noise. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag; pilot enabled for 10% of traffic on main for 48 hours, inspect alerts and costs, then increase to 50% and finally global; rollback via feature flag. Links: design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-5621/token-level-observability; related follow-up: ENG-5690 (alert automation).

review_comments: Diego Morales (reviewer): Can we clarify the default sampling rate rationale? At 0.1% are we confident we will catch regressions on low-volume routes?

Avery Chen (author): Default is intentional to keep cardinality/cost low in Hosted. We added a higher sampling path for Dedicated where customers can set 1-5% for pilot. Documentation updated with guidance.
Priya Nair (reviewer): Alert thresholds look conservative but I worry about noise during canary. Suggest a 48h burn-in window before enabling high-sensitivity alerts.
Avery Chen (author): Agree; rollout plan updated to include 48h pilot and a cooldown period in automation. Also added alert suppression during canary windows.
Sam Patel (reviewer): Integration tests are great. Noted a flaky e2e observability test on first run; re-ran CI and it passed. Consider increasing timeout on Prometheus scrape simulation.
Avery Chen (author): Increased timeout in test harness and added retry for eventual consistency checks.
